name: Cossack Hetmanate
native: Військо Запорозьке (Viisko Zaporozke, the Zaporozhian Host)

predecessors.name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
predecessors.text: the Kyiv, Bratslav and Chernihiv voivodeships, 'Cossack-held' after the Khmelnytsky Uprising (Zboriv, August 1649)

rulers.name: Petro Doroshenko
rulers.title: right-bank hetman 1665, sole hetman from 8 June 1668

rulers.name: Governing Council of the Hetman Office (no hetman)

ledger.x: 1648: Khmelnytsky's uprising founds the Cossack Hetmanate on the middle Dnieper.
May 1648: the Cossacks take the field.
19 August 1649: the Treaty of Zboriv ends the first war.
19 August 1649: Zboriv gives the Cossacks the Kyiv, Bratslav and Chernihiv voivodeships.
September 1658: Vyhovsky turns to Poland.
September 1659: Vyhovsky falls.
Late 1663: the Polish king invades the left bank. the Polish-Lithuanian king crossed the Dnieper and invaded left-bank Ukraine in late 1663; the siege of Hlukhiv failed in January 1664.
January 1667: the Truce of Andrusovo ends the fighting.
January 1667: Andrusovo cuts the Hetmanate in half along the Dnieper.
8-9 June 1668: Doroshenko proclaims a united Ukraine.
1669: the capital moves from Chyhyryn to Baturyn.
1672: the Ottomans take the right bank.
6 May 1686: the Eternal Peace leaves the Sich 'nominally dependent both on the hetman and the tsar'.
6 May 1686: the Hetmanate's right-bank land leaves with the division, so the occupation entry ends here.

6 May 1686: the Treaty of Perpetual Peace ('signed in Moscow on 6 May 1686') 'secured Russia's possession of left-bank Ukraine, plus the right-bank city of Kiev', and 'Poland retained right-bank Ukraine'; the Hetmanate page says the treaty 'established the division of the Hetmanate'.
13 November 1708: Russia strikes the Hetmanate.
November 1708: the capital moves to Hlukhiv.
May 1709: the Sich is destroyed.
8 July 1709: Poltava ends Mazepa's revolt.
21 October 1764: the left-bank land passes to Russia on the decree, not from 1721.
21 October 1764: Catherine II abolishes the hetmanate.

wars.name: Khmelnytsky Uprising
wars.outcome: Cossack victory: Zboriv (19 August 1649) gave autonomy to the Kyiv, Bratslav and Chernihiv voivodeships; after Berestechko (28 June 1651) Bila Tserkva limited the register to 20,000 and autonomy to the Kyiv voivodeship; peace on 17 December 1653 after…

wars.name: Russo-Polish War (1654-1667)
wars.outcome: Truce of Andrusovo, January 1667: the Commonwealth ceded Smolensk and left-bank Dnieper Ukraine, including Kiev, to Russia and kept right-bank Ukraine, dividing the Hetmanate along the Dnieper.

wars.name: The Ruin
wars.outcome: Civil wars after Khmelnytsky's death (6 August 1657) to Mazepa's ascension (1687): partition in 1663, Doroshenko's united hetmanate of 9 June 1668, Ottoman suzerainty of 1669, the Ottoman occupation of 1672-1699, Doroshenko's capitulation in 1676 and the…

wars.name: Mazepa's revolt (Great Northern War, Ukrainian front)
wars.outcome: Mazepa allied with Charles XII on 28 October 1708, Baturyn was sacked on 13 November, the Swedes lost at Poltava on 8 July 1709; Mazepa died at Bender on 2 October 1709 and the Hetmanate's autonomy became nominal.

certainty.note: The Hetmanate was a de facto frontier state on the steppe edge; only the voivodeship names of Zboriv define it, with no surveyed line.
The Dnieper line against the Commonwealth is treaty-fixed by Andrusovo (1667) and the Eternal Peace (1686) but the Russian, Sloboda and steppe limits are not.
